answers.value: The full in-force delegated-authority book written by all active coverholders, MGAs and TPAs, tested against each binder's limits in the Delegated Authority Matrix v4.1: per-risk limit, aggregate premium cap, prohibited/no-write classes, and territory restrictions. Scope = every bound risk in the current bordereaux load.
The current monthly bordereaux reporting period (e.g. bind dates 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30); risks bound outside the period are excluded and picked up in their own cycle.

Each bound risk carries coverholder code, LOB, limit, premium, effective date and class code; the matrix rule engine flags any field breaching a binder limit. Risks with missing limit or class code are quarantined as data-quality exceptions before the breach test runs.

Bordereaux risk count and premium sum reconcile to the coverholder's declared totals and to PolicyCenter postings; delta must be 0. Any variance over 1% of premium is logged and blocks sign-off until resolved.

The breach/appetite exception report is exported to Archer GRC as a dated 'DA-Breach' record and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/ with version label and run timestamp; retained per the 7-year underwriting-file policy.

Each flagged breach or out-of-appetite risk is opened as an Archer 'DA-Breach' item with disposition (within-tolerance / remediate / escalate), owner and target date; unresolved material breaches auto-route to the escalation task within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Test every bound risk against the coverholder's premium, limit and LOB authority in the matrix
checklist.value: The Archer rule set encodes Delegated Authority Matrix v4.1 limits per binder; each bordereaux row is evaluated against per-risk limit, aggregate premium cap and permitted LOB.

testing.step: Confirm no bound risk exceeds its binder authority
testing.value: 0 risks bound above per-risk limit, aggregate cap or outside permitted LOB pass without a flagged breach; sample 25 flagged rows per month reconcile to the matrix.

checklist.step: Apply documented referral triggers to detect risks that should have been referred
checklist.value: Breach logic includes referral-trigger thresholds (large limits, cat-exposed territory, prohibited class) so unreferred risks surface as out-of-appetite flags.

testing.value: For 100% of risks hitting a referral trigger, a referral record exists in PolicyCenter; any missing referral is logged as a breach.

checklist.step: Preserve a full audit trail of the breach-detection run
checklist.value: Run parameters, matrix version, input bordereaux and output exception list are captured in Archer with immutable timestamp.

testing.value: Every breach run has a retrievable trail showing inputs, matrix version and reviewer; 0 runs without a stored trail.

answers.value: Material breaches of delegated-authority limits identified in the aggregate book — those exceeding the materiality threshold (single risk >125% of per-risk limit, or aggregate premium >110% of binder cap, or any prohibited-class bind) — that require escalation to underwriting management or the Delegated Authority Committee.
The current monthly oversight cycle; breaches are escalated within 2 business days of being flagged, with the committee pack compiled for the next monthly DA governance meeting.

Each escalation record carries coverholder, breach type, quantum vs limit, financial exposure, recommended action and sign-off route; records missing quantum or recommended action are returned to the analyst before escalation.
Count of material breaches escalated reconciles to the breach register: every Archer item flagged 'material' has a matching committee escalation; delta must be 0 at cycle close.

The escalation memo and committee minutes are stored in Archer against the DA-Breach record and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Escalations/ with timestamp and version.
Breaches the committee accepts are logged with an approved rationale and expiry; those requiring action get a remediation item with a 10-business-day SLA and re-escalation if breached.
All breaches classified 'material' in the current cycle (census, not a sample) plus a look-back over any prior-cycle material breaches still open.

PASS = 100% of material breaches escalated within the 2-business-day SLA with a complete record and committee disposition. FAIL = any material breach unescalated, escalated late, or lacking a documented decision.
Late or incomplete escalations raise an Archer 'SLA-Miss' item to the CUO with root cause; recurring misses trigger a review of the DA monitoring workflow.

Escalation routing follows the Delegated Authority Matrix v4.1 delegation table: manager-level breaches to the Delegated Authority Manager, material/prohibited-class breaches to the CUO and the DA Committee; the matrix is version-controlled in Archer.

Acceptance criteria: every material breach escalated within the 2-business-day SLA with a complete record and a documented committee disposition. Evidence = the Archer escalation record and committee minutes, archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Escalations/.

checklist.step: Route material breaches for CUO approval with full documentation
checklist.value: Any acceptance of a material authority breach requires a documented CUO decision captured in the Archer escalation record before the risk is retained.

testing.step: Verify CUO sign-off on accepted breaches
testing.value: 100% of accepted material breaches carry a CUO approval with rationale; 0 accepted without documented authority-level sign-off.

checklist.step: Escalate to the next authority level with a recommendation
checklist.value: Each escalation memo states the breach, options and a recommended action, addressed to the correct authority tier per the delegation matrix.

testing.value: Every committee escalation includes a named recommendation and reaches the correct authority level; sample 10 escalations per quarter for completeness.

answers.value: Coverholders/binders whose portfolio performance has deteriorated beyond tolerance — loss ratio above the agreed threshold, adverse frequency trend, or repeated authority breaches — that warrant capacity reduction or authority withdrawal. Scope = binders breaching the performance triggers in the current review.
Rolling 12-month loss experience as at the current quarter-end (e.g. AY-to-date through 2026-06-30), compared against plan and the prior two review cycles.

Each binder record shows earned premium, incurred losses, loss ratio, trend and breach count; binders missing losses-to-date or premium are excluded from the deterioration test until the bordereaux is corrected.
Binder premium and loss totals reconcile to PolicyCenter and to actuarial reserves; loss-ratio figures used in the decision must tie to the quarterly reserving run within 1%.

The capacity-reduction decision memo, supporting loss triangles and the amended authority schedule are stored in Archer and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Capacity/ with version and timestamp.

A binder that breaches tolerance but is retained at current capacity requires a documented CUO exception with rationale and review date; otherwise a capacity-reduction or withdrawal action is opened with a 10-business-day SLA.

Loss-ratio and trend figures are produced from the approved quarterly reserving methodology (reserving model vQ2-2026) signed off by the Reserving Actuary; only that approved version feeds the deterioration test.

Sensitivity of the loss ratio to IBNR selection and large-loss treatment is documented; a +/-5 point loss-ratio swing under alternative assumptions is shown alongside the base case in the decision pack.

Materiality threshold for action = loss ratio >15 points above plan sustained over two quarters, or aggregate deterioration >USD 2m; thresholds are set in the DA performance policy and version-controlled.
All binders breaching the performance triggers in the current review (census of deteriorating binders); each assessed for a capacity-reduction or withdrawal decision.

PASS = every binder breaching tolerance has a documented decision (reduce / withdraw / retain-with-exception) supported by reconciled loss data. FAIL = a deteriorating binder with no decision, or a decision unsupported by the loss experience.

Retaining a deteriorating binder requires a documented CUO exception with review date; otherwise a capacity-reduction/withdrawal action is opened with a 10-business-day SLA and coverholder notification.
Acceptance criteria: loss data reconciled to reserving, tolerance breach quantified against the documented threshold, and CUO sign-off on the capacity action or exception before it is actioned.
Evidence = the capacity-reduction decision memo, loss triangles and amended authority schedule in Archer, archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Capacity/.

Materiality/tolerance thresholds = loss ratio >15 points above plan sustained over two quarters, or aggregate deterioration >USD 2m, per the DA performance policy; a binder breaching either triggers a capacity-reduction review.

Approved methodology/model = the quarterly reserving model vQ2-2026 signed off by the Reserving Actuary; parameters (development factors, IBNR selections, large-loss thresholds) sourced from the approved reserving parameter set for the current quarter.

checklist.step: Test performance against the documented appetite for the LOB/geography/industry
checklist.value: Deterioration is judged against the appetite thresholds documented for each binder's LOB and territory; out-of-appetite performance triggers capacity review.

testing.step: Verify appetite thresholds drive the decision
testing.value: Every capacity-reduction decision cites the specific appetite/loss threshold breached; 0 actions taken without a documented threshold.

checklist.step: Compare binder loss ratio to the LOB target
checklist.value: Each binder's rolling loss ratio is measured against the loss-ratio target for its line of business, sourced from plan.

testing.value: Binders flagged for reduction show loss ratio above the LOB target by the documented margin; figures reconcile to reserving.

checklist.step: Obtain CUO approval where capacity is retained despite a breach
checklist.value: Retaining a deteriorating binder at full capacity requires a documented CUO exception in Archer with rationale and review date.

testing.value: 100% of retained out-of-tolerance binders carry a CUO exception; 0 undocumented retentions.

answers.value: The register of active coverholders, MGAs and TPAs with each entity's binder reference, delegated authority limits, permitted LOB/territory, effective and expiry dates, and due-diligence status. Scope = all binders currently in force plus those expiring within 90 days.
Continuously maintained; a full reconciliation is performed monthly and the register is dated as current at each month-end (e.g. as at 2026-06-30).

Each register row must carry binder ID, entity legal name, authority limits, LOB/territory, effective/expiry dates and current due-diligence flag; rows missing expiry date or limits are flagged red and cannot be marked active.
Active-binder count in the register reconciles to executed binder agreements in OpenText and to open coverholder codes in PolicyCenter; delta must be 0 at month-end reconciliation.

The register snapshot is versioned and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Register/ at each month-end with timestamp; supporting binder agreements retained in OpenText for the binder life plus 7 years.

Expired or lapsed-due-diligence binders left flagged active are logged as exceptions and either renewed, suspended or removed within 10 business days; suspensions are notified to the Coverholder Coordinator.
All register entries (census) reconciled against source binder agreements at month-end; expiring-within-90-days binders receive a targeted check.

PASS = every active binder in the register matches an executed, in-date agreement with current due diligence and correct limits. FAIL = any active row with expired agreement, stale due diligence, or limits not matching the signed binder.
Mismatches raise an OpenText/Archer exception; the Coverholder Coordinator obtains the corrected agreement or the entity is suspended until resolved.

Field definitions follow the DA register data dictionary: binder_id, entity_name, authority_limit, permitted_lob, territory, effective_date, expiry_date, dd_status — sourced from the executed binder agreement.
Control total = number of executed in-force binder agreements in OpenText; reconciles to active register rows with 0 variance at month-end.

In-scope effective dates = each binder's effective date through its expiry/renewal date; the register is reconciled and dated current as at each month-end (e.g. 2026-06-30), with binders expiring within 90 days surfaced for renewal action.

checklist.step: Record each binder's authority limits by premium, limit and LOB in the register
checklist.value: Register captures per-binder authority limits, permitted LOB and territory exactly as executed in the binder agreement.

testing.step: Verify register limits match executed binders
testing.value: Sample 25 binders per quarter; register limits reconcile 1:1 to the signed agreement; 0 discrepancies.

checklist.step: Maintain an audit trail of register changes
checklist.value: Every add/amend/suspend action is logged with user, timestamp and prior value in the register change log.

testing.value: 100% of register changes have a logged actor and timestamp; 0 unattributed edits.

answers.value: Production volumes (bound premium and risk counts) by coverholder/binder measured against each binder's premium capacity and aggregate limits, plus any per-peril or per-territory sub-limits. Scope = all active binders in the current reporting period.
Year-to-date against the current underwriting year, refreshed monthly on receipt of the coverholder bordereaux (e.g. YTD to 2026-06-30).
Each binder line shows written premium YTD, capacity, utilization %, and risk count vs limit; binders with missing capacity figures are flagged and excluded from the utilization ranking.
Written-premium totals from the bordereaux reconcile to PolicyCenter postings for the period; utilization is recomputed only after the reconciliation ties to within 1%.

The monthly utilization report is published to the Power BI 'Delegated Authority Oversight' dashboard and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Utilization/ with version and run timestamp.

Binders exceeding 90% capacity utilization raise an early-warning exception to the Delegated Authority Manager; binders over 100% raise a breach item routed to the escalation task within 2 business days.
All active binders in the reporting period (census); each measured for utilization against its capacity and sub-limits.
PASS = utilization computed for 100% of active binders and all breaches/near-limits flagged and routed. FAIL = any binder without a utilization figure, or an over-limit binder not flagged.
Binders over sub-limit or aggregate cap generate an exception with recommended action (pause binding / renegotiate capacity); unactioned exceptions re-escalate after 10 business days.

Acceptance criteria: every active binder has a current utilization %, near-limit (>90%) and over-limit (>100%) binders are flagged, and the dashboard refresh completes for the period with reconciled premium.

Evidence = Power BI utilization report plus the reconciliation workbook, archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Utilization/ and linked from the monthly DA oversight pack.

checklist.step: Measure production against each binder's premium and limit authority
checklist.value: Utilization is computed against the binder capacity and aggregate limits recorded in the Delegated Authority Matrix v4.1.

testing.step: Confirm utilization tied to matrix capacity
testing.value: Sampled binders' utilization denominators equal the matrix capacity; 0 mismatches.

checklist.step: Trigger referral when utilization thresholds are hit
checklist.value: Near-limit (>90%) and over-limit binders trigger the documented referral/escalation path automatically.

testing.value: Inject a test binder over 100% capacity; confirm an exception is raised and routed to the DA Manager.

answers.value: The coverholder/binder leads who must receive the relevant aggregate oversight findings for their portfolio — utilization warnings, breach notices, loss-ratio deterioration and required remediation actions. Scope = leads for every binder with an open finding in the current cycle.
The current monthly oversight cycle; notifications issue within 2 business days of the finding being confirmed.
Each notification records recipient, binder reference, finding summary, required action and due date; notifications missing a recipient or an action are held until completed.
Count of notifications sent reconciles to the count of open findings assigned to a coverholder lead; every finding requiring communication has a matching sent notice (delta = 0).
Sent notifications and acknowledgements are stored against the PolicyCenter binder activity and copied to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Comms/ with timestamp.
Notifications not acknowledged within 5 business days are re-sent and escalated to the Coverholder Coordinator; unresolved acknowledgements are logged as exceptions.

checklist.step: Keep an audit trail of findings communicated to coverholder leads
checklist.value: Each notification is logged with recipient, content, timestamp and acknowledgement against the binder record.

testing.value: 100% of open findings requiring notice have a logged, timestamped notification; 0 findings closed as 'notified' without evidence.

checklist.step: Document the finding, recipient and required action in the file
checklist.value: The notification content, named recipient and action/due date are recorded in the binder file and the DA comms folder.

testing.value: Sample 15 notifications per quarter; each has recipient, finding and action documented; 0 incomplete records.

answers.value: Delegated-authority performance reports for Lloyd's or carrier oversight and governance bodies: binder-level premium, loss ratio, utilization, breach and remediation status across the active DA book, plus the aggregate portfolio view. Scope = all active binders for the reporting quarter.
The reporting quarter just closed (e.g. Q2 2026, through 2026-06-30), with prior-period and plan comparatives.
Every report section is populated — premium, loss ratio, utilization, breach counts, remediation status — with binder and period identifiers; a report with any mandatory KPI blank cannot be issued.
Report premium and loss totals reconcile to PolicyCenter and the quarterly reserving run; the aggregate figures tie to the sum of binder-level lines with 0 variance.

The issued report (PDF plus Power BI export) is versioned and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Reports/ with timestamp; retained 7 years for regulatory/Lloyd's examination.

Data-quality gaps or late bordereaux that prevent a complete report are logged as exceptions with the affected binders noted; the report is issued with a documented caveat and the gap remediated next cycle.
The full quarterly report pack (census of all active binders plus the aggregate view); reviewed before release to governance bodies.

PASS = all mandatory KPIs present, aggregate ties to binder detail, figures reconcile to source systems, and the report is signed off before the reporting deadline. FAIL = any missing KPI, reconciliation break, or missed deadline.
Reconciliation breaks or missing KPIs block issue; the analyst corrects and re-runs, or issues with a documented, DA-Manager-approved caveat and a remediation item.

KPI definitions follow the DA reporting data dictionary: written_premium, earned_premium, incurred_loss, loss_ratio, utilization_pct, breach_count, remediation_status — sourced from PolicyCenter and reserving.
Control total = binder-level premium and loss lines summing to the aggregate portfolio figures on the report cover; reconciles to PolicyCenter with 0 variance.

Acceptance criteria: complete KPI set, binder-to-aggregate reconciliation, and sign-off by the Delegated Authority Manager before the governance deadline. Evidence = the issued report plus reconciliation workbook, archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/DA-Oversight/<YYYY-Qn>/Reports/ and linked in the governance pack.

checklist.step: Report binder loss ratios against LOB targets
checklist.value: Each binder's loss ratio is shown against its LOB target so governance can see performance versus plan.

testing.value: Sampled binder loss ratios reconcile to reserving output; 0 unreconciled figures in the issued report.

checklist.step: Provide DA performance evidence to support internal audit
checklist.value: The quarterly report and its reconciliations are retained in a form suitable for internal audit and Lloyd's/carrier examination.

testing.value: For a sampled quarter, the report, source reconciliations and sign-off are all retrievable from the archive; 0 missing artefacts.

checklist.step: Preserve an audit trail for each issued report
checklist.value: Report version, data cut date, author and approver are logged with the archived report.

testing.value: Every issued report has a version, timestamp and approver on record; 0 reports without a trail.

answers.value: Aggregate delegated-authority exposure — accumulations by peril, zone, class and coverholder — reviewed against treaty retention/limit structure and company risk-tolerance thresholds. Scope = the whole DA book's modelled and booked aggregate as at the review date.
Quarter-end aggregate position (e.g. as at 2026-06-30), compared to the prior quarter and to the reinsurance treaty year in force.

Exposure records carry TIV/limit, peril, zone, class and coverholder; the review requires modelled PML/AAL alongside treaty retention and company tolerance. Records lacking geocode or limit are excluded from the accumulation and flagged.
Aggregate exposure summed from the risk detail reconciles to PolicyCenter in-force and to the cat-model input file; sums must tie within 1% before the tolerance comparison is made.

The review memo, accumulation output and tolerance comparison are versioned and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/Exposure/<YYYY-Qn>/ with timestamp; retained for treaty-review and regulatory examination.

Any zone/peril breaching the company tolerance or treaty limit is logged as an exception with a recommended action (purchase fac, reduce binding, adjust appetite) and routed to the CUO for decision within 5 business days.
All modelled peril/zone accumulations across the DA book (census); the highest accumulations and any near-tolerance zones receive detailed review.

PASS = every zone/peril accumulation is within company tolerance and treaty limits, or a documented exception exists. FAIL = any accumulation over tolerance/treaty limit without an approved exception or mitigation.
Over-tolerance accumulations trigger a mitigation plan (fac purchase, capacity pause) with a named owner and date; unresolved breaches re-escalate to the CUO and the risk committee.
Acceptance criteria: reconciled aggregate, every peril/zone measured against company tolerance and treaty structure, and CUO sign-off on any exception before the review closes.
Evidence = accumulation output, tolerance-comparison memo and CUO decisions, archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/Exposure/<YYYY-Qn>/ and linked in the quarterly exposure pack.

Materiality/tolerance thresholds = the company risk-tolerance limits per peril/zone (e.g. single-zone PML within net treaty retention plus the board-approved appetite buffer) documented in the exposure-management policy and version-controlled; breaches above threshold trigger escalation.

checklist.step: Compare aggregate exposure to the documented appetite by LOB/geography
checklist.value: Accumulations are tested against the documented appetite limits per peril, zone and LOB set in the exposure policy.

testing.value: Every reviewed accumulation cites its appetite/tolerance limit; 0 zones assessed without a documented threshold.

checklist.step: Route over-tolerance exposure for CUO approval
checklist.value: Any accumulation retained above tolerance requires a documented CUO exception with mitigation and review date.

testing.value: 100% of over-tolerance accumulations carry a CUO exception or mitigation; 0 undocumented retentions.

checklist.step: Enforce the no-write list within the aggregate view
checklist.value: Prohibited zones/classes on the no-write list are checked in the accumulation; any bound risk in a no-write area is flagged.

testing.value: 0 bound risks in no-write zones/classes pass the review unflagged; sample 25 high-accumulation risks per quarter.

answers.value: The aggregate delegated-authority exposure dashboard: current accumulations by peril/zone/class/coverholder, utilization vs limits, and tolerance headroom. Scope = the full active DA book feeding the Power BI 'DA Exposure' dashboard.
Refreshed to the latest data cut (monthly on bordereaux receipt, with an intra-month refresh after any large bind); dashboard as-at date stamped at each refresh.
The dashboard load requires exposure, limit and geocode fields per risk; rows failing validation are quarantined and shown as a data-quality count so users know the coverage of the refresh.
Dashboard totals reconcile to the source PolicyCenter in-force extract and the prior refresh; premium and exposure control totals must tie within 1% or the refresh is held.
Each refresh is versioned with an as-at date and the input extract archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/Exposure/<YYYY-Qn>/Dashboard/ so any published view can be reproduced.
A failed or partial refresh raises an exception; the dashboard shows a stale-data banner with the last good as-at date until the load is corrected within 1 business day.

checklist.step: Surface exposure against documented appetite on the dashboard
checklist.value: The dashboard shows accumulations against the documented appetite/tolerance limits per peril and zone.

testing.value: Sampled zones show the correct tolerance limit and headroom; 0 mislabelled thresholds after refresh.

checklist.step: Keep an audit trail of dashboard refreshes
checklist.value: Each refresh logs as-at date, source extract and reconciliation status so any view is reproducible.

testing.value: A sampled historical as-at view can be reproduced from the archived extract; 0 irreproducible refreshes.

answers.value: Claim frequency and severity trends sliced by class, geography, construction type and customer segment across the underwriting portfolio, to inform appetite and pricing signals. Scope = the in-force and recently-lapsed book with matched claims experience.
A rolling look-back of at least the last 12 accident quarters through the current quarter-end (e.g. 2023-Q3 to 2026-Q2) to give a stable trend signal.

Each exposure/claim record needs class, geocode, construction/segment tag, earned exposure and incurred loss; records missing segment tags are grouped as 'unclassified' and reported separately so trends are not distorted.
Earned exposure and incurred losses used in the trend reconcile to PolicyCenter and the quarterly reserving run; segment sub-totals sum to the portfolio total with 0 variance.
The trend analysis workbook and Power BI views are versioned and archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/Performance/<YYYY-Qn>/Trends/ with data cut date and timestamp.

Anomalous segments (frequency or severity moving beyond the control band) are flagged with a hypothesis and referred to pricing/appetite review; data anomalies are logged and corrected before conclusions are finalised.
Trend methodology (exposure-adjusted frequency and severity with credibility weighting) is the approved portfolio-analytics method v2026.1, signed off by the Pricing Actuary before use.
Sensitivity of trend selections to development-factor and large-loss thresholds is documented; frequency/severity trends are shown at low/central/high development to bound the estimate.
Materiality threshold for action = a segment trend more than 2 standard deviations from portfolio, or a >10% severity shift sustained over two quarters, documented in the analytics standard.
Sampled aggregated segment figures trace back to individual claim and policy records in ClaimCenter/PolicyCenter; 25 sampled data points per quarter reconcile to source screens.
Claim status (open/closed/reopened) aligns to the reserving workflow so severity uses appropriately developed incurred amounts; open-claim development is handled per the reserving basis.
Accident date, report date and transaction date align to the accident-quarter definition used in the trend so exposure and losses are matched to the correct period.
The full segment matrix (class x geography x construction/segment) over the look-back window; each cell with credible exposure is trended.

PASS = trend re-run reproduces the reported frequency/severity within tolerance, segment sub-totals reconcile, and flagged segments are supported by the data. FAIL = irreproducible trend, reconciliation break, or an unsupported conclusion.
Low-credibility cells are grouped up to a credible level rather than over-interpreted; data anomalies are logged and excluded with rationale, and the analysis re-run.
Portfolio-analytics trend method v2026.1 (exposure-adjusted, credibility-weighted) as approved by the Pricing Actuary.
Parameters (development factors, trend seeds, large-loss thresholds) sourced from the approved reserving parameter set for the current quarter.

Acceptance criteria: reconciled exposure/loss inputs, trends produced with the approved method and parameters, and Pricing Actuary review of material segment findings. Evidence = the trend workbook and Power BI views, archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/Performance/<YYYY-Qn>/Trends/ and linked in the portfolio review pack.

testing.value: Each flagged segment shows its trend impact on the LOB loss ratio versus target; 0 findings without a target reference.

checklist.value: Segments trending adversely are referred to appetite review so the documented appetite by LOB/geography can be adjusted.

Segments materially off benchmark (variance beyond the control band) are flagged with commentary and referred to portfolio/pricing review; comparator or index gaps are logged and sourced before the pack is finalised.
All LOB/segment benchmark lines for the quarter (census); segments with the largest variance to plan or market receive detailed commentary.

PASS = every segment benchmarked against plan, prior year and market where available, actuals reconciled, and material variances explained. FAIL = missing comparator without a 'no benchmark' note, reconciliation break, or unexplained material variance.
Unexplained variances are escalated to the Portfolio UW Manager with a hypothesis and follow-up owner; index/comparator sourcing gaps are remediated the next cycle.
Acceptance criteria: reconciled actuals, plan and prior-year comparatives loaded, market indices applied where available, and Portfolio UW Manager review of material variances.

Evidence = the benchmarking pack, reconciliation workbook and index source records, archived to SharePoint /Underwriting/Portfolio/Performance/<YYYY-Qn>/Benchmark/ and linked in the portfolio review pack.

Field definitions follow the portfolio-performance data dictionary: written_premium, earned_premium, incurred_loss, loss_ratio, retention_pct, hit_ratio, plan_value, prior_year_value, market_index — actuals sourced from PolicyCenter/reserving, plan from the approved plan file, indices from the licensed market data source. Control total = segment lines summing to the portfolio total, reconciled with 0 variance.

checklist.step: Benchmark loss ratio against the LOB target and market
checklist.value: Each LOB's loss ratio is compared to its plan target and the market loss index for the period.

testing.value: Sampled LOB loss ratios reconcile to reserving and are shown against target and index; 0 unreconciled or unbenchmarked lines.

checklist.step: Benchmark hit ratio against segment targets
checklist.value: Hit ratio by segment is compared to the target hit ratio to assess conversion performance.

testing.value: Every segment shows hit ratio against target; underperforming segments are flagged for review.

checklist.step: Benchmark retention against segment targets
checklist.value: Retention rate by segment is compared to the target retention to assess book stability.

testing.value: Each segment shows retention against target; segments below target are flagged with commentary.
